t: Minimum Cost to Repair Edges to Traverse a Graph
o: Pick a threshold money; every edge with cost ≤ money becomes usable. Reach node n-1 from node 0 using at most k edges (hop count, not weighted length), minimizing money; return -1 if impossible. Example 1: with k = 1 only the direct 0-2 edge works, costing 100. Example 2: threshold 12 unlocks 0→1→5 (2 hops); nothing cheaper admits a ≤ 2-hop path. Example 3: node 2 is disconnected regardless. The answer is always one of the edge weights (or 0), so binary search the threshold and check feasibility with a hop-limited BFS.
k: Monotone feasibility in money makes binary search over sorted distinct edge weights valid.
Feasibility check = BFS counting hops (unweighted), ignoring edges heavier than the threshold.

a.n: Binary Search on Threshold + Hop-Limited BFS
a.i: Sort distinct weights; for a candidate limit run BFS from node 0 expanding only edges with w ≤ limit and at most k levels; feasible iff node n-1 gets a distance ≤ k. Feasibility is monotone (more money only adds edges), so binary search finds the minimal weight; if even the maximum fails, return -1.
s: Collect and sort distinct edge weights.
Binary search: for mid limit, BFS from 0 with dist[] initialized to -1, expanding neighbors via edges with w ≤ limit and dist < k.
If dist[n-1] != -1, feasible — try smaller; else try larger.
Return the smallest feasible weight, or -1 if none.
a.t: O((n + m) log m) — each BFS is O(n + m) and binary search performs O(log m) of them
a.sp: O(n + m) — adjacency list and distance array

w: Emphasize why the answer lives in the weight set (money only matters through which edges it unlocks) and why plain BFS suffices (edge usage is binary, hop limit replaces weights). Pitfall: confusing the hop limit k with path cost — do not run Dijkstra; and stopping BFS expansion at depth k correctly (nodes at depth k are reached but not expanded). Edge cases: n - 1 == 0 style trivial reachability, disconnected graphs returning -1. Follow-up: minimize money and then hops among ties, or dynamic edge failures.
